newsitem.title: USA: U2 gives world tour details at New York's Kmart.
newsitem.headline: U2 gives world tour details at New York's Kmart.

text.p: The Irish band U2 on Wednesday announced the details of its worldwide "PopMart" tour, one of the biggest rock extravaganzas ever, at a news conference in a downtown Manhattan discount store's lingerie department.

"We believe in trash. We believe in kitsch, and that's what we're up to at the moment," the band's guitarist Edge told reporters at the recently opened Kmart, the first Manhattan outlet for the third biggest U.S. retailer.
The elaborate U2 tour of more than 100 shows, many in outdoor venues or giant stadiums, kicks off on April 25 in Las Vegas and ends more than a year later after stops all over the world.

Producer Michael Cohl, who has produced such shows as the Rolling Stones' "Voodoo Lounge" and "Steel Wheels" tours, said he expects 5 million to 6 million people to attend the shows. He has projected the tour could gross $260 million.
Bono, the band's popular vocalist, warned the show's production costs would be high too. "It costs a fortune to look this trashy," he said.
It is the Grammy-winning Dublin-based band's first tour in almost four years and coincides with the release of its new album "Pop" next month.
To the delight of Kmart shoppers who crowded around to listen, the band played "Holy Joe," a new song featured on the album.
Asked why the band chose Kmart to make its announcement, the leather-clad Bono joked that he couldn't remember, but "it made a lot of sense at the time."
Peppered with questions about using the discount chain, which has most of its stores in suburban malls, he finally said to one reporter, "Don't be such a snob, really."
The band's manager denied published reports that U2 needed investors to finance its ambitious tour.
"If we could get someone to give us a lot of money and not have to kiss ass, we would take it," Bono said. "Unfortunately we haven't figured that out."

The band has made such popular albums as "The Joshua Tree" in 1987, with the singles "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking for" and "With or Without You"; "Rattle and Hum" in 1988 with the hit "All I Want Is You"; "Achtung Baby" in 1991 and "Zooropa" in 1993.
Band members also worked on the soundtrack for the movies "Batman Forever," "Goldeneye" and "Mission:Impossible."
